claims.statement: Anomaly-oriented malware detection has a demonstrated implementation pathway: AProctor directly evaluates anomaly detection on Android and reports high malware detection rates, including temporally different and previously unseen APKs, demonstrating that anomaly-style behavioral detection can be implemented as an on-device malware defense.

Anomaly-based malware detection has a direct deployment limitation: anomaly algorithms can consume substantial energy and computing resources on constrained devices, and the proposed design required feature reduction and server-side training before on-device use.

NIST behavioral anomaly detection guidance documents BAD implementation and testing in ICS/manufacturing contexts, including configuration for packet-stream visibility, file-transfer alerting, and integration with existing tools, processes, and system infrastructure.

The frozen deployment context is a CIS IG2 reference enterprise profile with multi-department enterprise IT, personnel responsible for managing and protecting infrastructure, and safeguards that may depend on enterprise-grade technology and specialized expertise.

conditional_requirements: If constrained devices are in scope, plan for energy and computing-resource limits, feature reduction, and server-side training before on-device deployment. (AE02C_E333FEC17F65B4E1)

A deployment-specific technical feasibility conclusion requires exact device classes, resource limits, available telemetry/log data, and integration path with existing tools, processes, and system infrastructure. (DE_DE05_105D0030778F41BC, CTX_CIS_IG2_9F94838146D9C3A4)

If unsupervised anomaly detection is used, assess adversarial robustness, including poisoning resistance, because poisoning of unsupervised learning for network traffic anomaly detection has been demonstrated. (E_15_D3680C31BEE2C0F8)
constraints: Anomaly-based detection may require feature reduction and server-side training before on-device use due to energy and computing-resource constraints on constrained devices. (AE02C_E333FEC17F65B4E1)

Deployment-specific operability depends on integration with existing tools, processes, and system infrastructure, which are not specified in the supplied context. (DE_DE05_105D0030778F41BC, CTX_CIS_IG2_9F94838146D9C3A4)

The reference-enterprise profile indicates possible dependence on enterprise-grade technology and specialized expertise, but exact staffing, vendor, product, or architecture details are absent. (CTX_CIS_IG2_9F94838146D9C3A4)
evidence_gaps: No supplied evidence identifies the exact target architecture, network segmentation, telemetry sources, or integration points for anomaly detection in the frozen CIS IG2 enterprise. (CTX_CIS_IG2_9F94838146D9C3A4)
No supplied evidence establishes whether anomaly detection is deployed or effective in the edge-device/custom-malware environment described in the Mandiant record. (E_03_F1CA4CD00581F628)
No supplied evidence establishes that a specific anomaly-detection implementation would be robust to poisoning attacks demonstrated for network traffic anomaly detection. (E_15_D3680C31BEE2C0F8)
assessment.rationale: The supplied records support general technical feasibility of ANOMALY DETECTION for malware because an action-specific technical_enablement record directly demonstrates anomaly-oriented malware detection implemented on-device, including detection of previously unseen APKs. An action-specific technical_limitation record also identifies a real barrier: substantial energy and computing-resource consumption on constrained devices, requiring feature reduction and server-side training before on-device use. On balance, the enablement evidence is more direct to the core technical capability, while the limitation evidence is a deployment-conditioned burden rather than a universal blocker. Deployment-specific compatibility remains insufficient because exact architecture, device resource limits, telemetry availability, integration points, and staffing/expertise details are not supplied.

equivalence_key: Multi-department enterprise IT with personnel responsible for managing and protecting infrastructure; the environment may require enterprise-grade technology and specialized expertise for some safeguards.

No numeric budget, price, ROI, TCO, staffing count, or procurement ceiling is assumed. Resource capacity is represented only by the frozen CIS IG2 reference profile; exact financial quantities remain unknown.
